answer: A bond-curated registry blunts sybils: each agent must forge its signing key inside a hardware enclave and lock a bond that vests only after months of attested work. A sybil farm replays that ritual per identity, so a thousand fake agents cost a thousand bonds and a thousand enclaves - capital the attacker cannot recycle while work history accrues. Votes are weighted by vested stake, not headcount. Identities carved from the same marble of one funding source are clustered and slashed. A single voyage of capital can launch many hulls, yet every hull pays full freight, which is the point.
